Very disappointing experience with two Porsche centres including Solihull and Nottingham.

I purchased my Porsche from Porsche Nottingham and within the first three months have experienced several maintenance issues. Most significantly, I was sold the car with brake pads that subsequently required replacement.

Following advice from Porsche GB, I took the car to Porsche Solihull, which is my nearest Porsche Centre, to have the issue assessed. The brake pads were confirmed as requiring replacement. I was advised that Porsche Solihull would liase with Porsche GB to have new brake pads fitted and have since heard nothing.

I reported the matter to Porsche GB expecting them to take ownership and resolve an issue with a car that I had purchased from a Porsche Centre. Unfortunately, despite this now being ongoing for around eight weeks, I still have absolutely no resolution.

What is particularly disappointing is that I bought the car from a Porsche main dealer expecting the quality, preparation and after-sales support associated with a premium brand. Instead, I have been left chasing Porsche GB and the dealerships myself.

Eight weeks later, I am still waiting for Porsche to resolve an issue that should never have arisen in the first place.

The Porsche brand is seriously overhyped. The premium price and badge are supposed to come with a premium level of service, but that certainly hasn’t been my experience. Save your money and go to a different brand, that’s what I’ll be doing next time I purchase a car
Part department is a joke been waiting 3 days just for a call back to get a price on some parts  and still not had one. So ended up ordering the parts from Porsche Lecister who where amazing

I'm not one to complain unless it's deserved and I believe it is now deserved.
I have multiple mental health conditions, one of which is Autism but because I look"normal" people don't know until I tell them.
I've had a few different customer service experiences whilst attending this establishment.
Last year I had double kidney surgery and I am no longer able to hold it when I need the toilet, so a few weeks ago I was waiting to be served by a barmaid and when they it came time to pay, I had to run to the toilet so I gave her a 10er and told her to keep the change. When I returned (to my wife of 20 years) the barmaid came over to us and made it out (without actually saying it) that I was tipping female staff behind my wife's back.
We had to spend the rest of the night with a middle aged creepy looking manager watching over us, like I was a danger to my wife or that she was in some sort of trouble.
This is a clear sign of visual/bias profiling.

Fast forward a couple of weeks and I mentioned this to a female manager (Dani), that because I'm mentally disabled but look normal that some of the staff had been off with me, she replied instantly, to let her know if any of the staff had been off with me. I initially thought it was nice to hear that someone was on my side.
Well we've been in 2 times since then and this Dani has avoided me. This is the whole "virtue signalling" stuff that also affects the majority of the 21st century population, they say they want to accept until they actually have to meet someone like "that".

Well today we went in and I noticed that drugs were being consumed in the toilet and on the way past Dani I mentioned it to her and because of who I am she completely blanked me.

So not only do these staff happily discriminate against people who don't "look" disabled, they are happy for drugs to be consumed on the premises as long as it's only reported by someone who's mentally disabled.

So to some it up, they discriminate against people with disabilities (as long as they don't look it) and are perfectly happy for drugs to consumed on the premises as long as a non-visible disabled person reports it

Very disappointing experience.

It is very easy for a business to take payment for a service, but extremely frustrating when the service you paid for is not actually carried out properly.

I booked and paid for a professional dental cleaning, but when I checked afterwards, I noticed that my back teeth had not been cleaned properly. I went to the reception and I felt that excuses were being made before the doctor was informed.

However, when the area was finally checked, I could actually see residue being removed from my teeth onto the hygienist’s glove. My teeth then had to be cleaned again.

Unfortunately, the experience at reception made the situation even worse. I needed a receipt for the amount I had paid, but I was told their machine was not working. I then had to wait a very long time, and rather than trying to find an alternative solution, I found the attitude at reception dismissive and unprofessional. I felt as though my concerns were being made light of rather than taken seriously.

I don’t expect perfection, but when I pay for a professional service, I expect the service to be completed properly. And when there is a problem, I expect it to be handled professionally and respectfully.

Sadly, based on both the quality of the cleaning and the way the situation was handled afterwards, I left extremely disappointed with my experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience with Invicta Motors Bolton

We found a Tesla Model 3 advertised on Autotrader and travelled over 60 miles to view it. The initial contact was good, and we appreciated them waiting for us after a motorway closure delayed our arrival.

The car was clearly still awaiting preparation. We identified several issues, including noisy front door hinges and doors that did not operate smoothly, missing plastic trim, significant glue residue where the kick plate should have been, peeling paint around the door seals, a dirty interior and bald tyres.

We paid a £500 deposit and agreed collection for the following Saturday. We were told the car had received a Tesla health check and that the issues identified would be dealt with before collection.

After repeatedly chasing for updates and the promised documentation, we were eventually told on Friday that the alloys still needed refurbishing. I specifically asked whether the tyres and other preparation work had been completed and was assured that they had, with the car having been in the workshop.

We therefore rearranged collection for Sunday and made another 60+ mile journey.
On arrival, we were told that the tyres had not been changed and the car could not be released. It then became apparent that many of the other issues we had identified on our first visit had also not been addressed. The door hinges were still noisy, the doors still didn't operate smoothly, the plastic trim and glue residue were still present, and the interior remained dirty. The battery was at just 17% and the car had travelled over 100 miles since our first visit.

We finally test drove the car and immediately noticed a loud creaking noise from the front passenger side, audible both inside and outside the vehicle.

The most disappointing aspect was not simply the condition of the car, but being given assurances that work had been completed when it clearly had not. We made 2x 120+ mile round trips based on those assurances.

Jordan has since apologised for our experience. To their credit, the dealership has refunded the £500 deposit within 24 hours and paid an additional £60 as a goodwill gesture towards the fuel costs.

I appreciate the apology and refund, but the whole experience was extremely frustrating and involved a significant amount of wasted time and travel.

I would recommend checking reviews on Trustpilot before travelling a long distance or paying a deposit. I wish I had done so before making the initial enquiry

one_star_reviews.text:
Our experience with Phillips & Cohen has been appalling.

I want to be very clear about the issue here. We dispute that this debt exists, but if Phillips & Cohen provides proper evidence showing that money is genuinely outstanding from my late grandmother's estate, it will be paid.

That has never been the problem.

The problem is the way this company has pursued members of a bereaved family, particularly my 70-year-old mother.

My grandmother died and, just three weeks later, my father died. My mother was therefore grieving the loss of her mother-in-law and her husband within the space of three weeks.

During that period, Phillips & Cohen began repeatedly contacting my mother regarding an alleged debt belonging to my late grandmother.

My mother was not the alleged debtor. She was not the executor. She was not responsible for probate and she had no authority or control over my grandmother's estate.

Despite this, she was repeatedly contacted about an alleged debt for which, to this day, we have not been provided any documentary evidence.

The calls became persistent enough that my mother blocked the number. Contact was then attempted from another number.

She eventually spoke to them and explained that her mother-in-law had died, that her own husband had died only three weeks later and that, to her knowledge, no money was owed.

More than a year later, the contact has started again.

I have now made a formal complaint and instructed Phillips & Cohen to cease all unsolicited contact with my mother, my 77-year-old aunt and every other member of our family. All communication is to come through me by email.

Their acknowledgement says the account has been placed on hold, yet the accompanying email says only that "standard contact" has been prevented and warns that we "may receive further contact" from another department.

That is not an adequate response to an explicit instruction to stop contacting the family.

Phillips & Cohen has now told us that the alleged debt relates to E.ON Next, but so far we have still been provided with no amount allegedly outstanding, no bill, no statement, no account history and no documentary evidence demonstrating that a debt actually exists.

We have also asked Phillips & Cohen to explain how they obtained the private contact details of my mother and my aunt in the first place.

If they had sufficient information to trace and repeatedly contact elderly, recently bereaved relatives, I would expect them to have had the basic details and evidence of the alleged debt available before doing so.

Again, if proper evidence establishes that money is genuinely owed by my grandmother's estate, it will be paid.

My complaint is not about avoiding a legitimate debt.

It is about the manner in which a 70-year-old grieving widow was pursued regarding somebody else's alleged liability when she had no authority over the estate, combined with the fact that no evidence of that alleged debt has ever been provided to us.

I described the conduct in my formal complaint as callous, unsympathetic and predatory.

Having considered their response, I stand by those words.

The formal complaint is ongoing and I will update this review when Phillips & Cohen provides its final response.

Essentially this firm are a bunch of grave robbers,  trying to make commission from utility companies chasing final bills... with 0 understanding or knowledge about the deceased estate or financial agreements in place with proper solicitors.

If you get a letter from Philip and Cohen... just remember to put it in the recycling bin so it can be used for something useful in future

one_star_reviews.text:
Honestly would never visit again. Before I go into the detail ill say that I fully understand problems happen, however, communication costs nothing and would have made the entire experience miles better.

I booked a table for 6 adults, a high chair and dog friendly. Now with having a young child and a dog placing us directly next to the live performer and also crammed into corner, it could not have been worse, my 16 month old instantly in tears from the noise. In addition to this there weren't even enough seats at the table for us, I had to ask and at which point the server moved an adjacent table to give us more room after I complained. Fair enough, move on right...

So i order the lamb as it sounds nice, sorry no lamb. Fine, i'll order the beef then. 50 minutes after we order (16 month old barely kept from screaming with the provisions we brought with us), a waitress comes over, sorry theres no beef left, you can have lamb, chicken or gammon....hang on, Lamb?

So firstly, why does it take 50 minutes for you to tell us that you dont have what we ordered and secondly why on earth were we then offered lamb which I was originally told there was none of...

So we all change our meals and it arrives 10 minutes later, so clearly not cooked fresh, just kept warm and dished up which begs the question why did it take so long in the first place. We then noticed that none of our meals had been served with the Yorkshire pudding..we asked, to then be told they had also run out.

Not enough cutlery for the 6 of us so another trip up to ask for more cutlery. By this point we are fuming and the poor waitress is profusely apologising, she is clearly embarrassed by the entire situation. She tells us she will speak to the manager about compensation (FYI we didnt ask for this but at this point I think it was a given).

We finish our meals and 30 minutes later still no show from the "manager" the waitress clears up and asks if the manager has been over..shes very embarrassed by this point when we tell her no.

Another server comes over, not the manager, and offers us deserts on the house. Mildly appreciated but nobody wanted deserts. We thanked him, apologised as we knew it wasn't his fault but we were just ready to leave.

At this point he says ok, he will get the bill!?!?! I mean given we had already been offered free deserts which we turned down, I think some financial compensation would have been offered anyway but offering to get the bill...WHEN WE PAID UPFRONT was just comical. I laughed and told him theres no way im paying for it twice, if anything I want my money back.

Overall, shit service, slow, poor quality food, only half the meal we paid for and no communication. Had we not paid upfront (where fyi i also tipped on both drink and food as I beleive bar staff deserve it!) I would have not paid a penny.

Frankly, ill never visit again and id advise everyone else to find somewhere else.

⭐ 1/5 – Absolutely appalling experience

From start to finish, my experience with Matthew Lettings has been horrendous.

Initially they were professional, convincing and said all the right things. Unfortunately, almost immediately after handing over my property, that professionalism disappeared.

I experienced repeated late rent payments, payment dates being changed without my agreement, issues with bills, missed appointments and maintenance that I was told had been completed when I later found it either hadn't been done or, in my opinion, had been completed poorly.

A major source of stress was Anup, my property manager. Communication eventually broke down completely. I found his manner rude, confrontational and extremely unpleasant. On one occasion he came into my personal space pointing his finger at me, which I found intimidating and completely inappropriate.

Things deteriorated so badly that it was agreed Matthew, the owner, would become my main point of contact instead. Unfortunately, this didn't improve matters. I continued struggling to get answers, with emails ignored and calls unanswered. I was also repeatedly given personal explanations, including bereavements and illness, for why matters couldn't be dealt with.

The situation became so stressful that I have had to take days off my own work simply to deal with this company and chase payments and answers.

The final month's rent was the final straw.

In one email I was told my rent hadn't been paid because of cash-flow problems. I was subsequently given a completely different explanation: that my rent was being withheld until seven days after the occupant left the property.

I repeatedly asked them to identify the specific clause in my agreement allowing them to withhold rent that was already due. I have still not received a satisfactory answer identifying that clause.
The owner of Mthew letts and the proparty manager Anup had actually blocked my number, meaning I was unable to call them at all. At the same time, my emails were also being ignored, leaving me with virtually no way of getting a response from the people responsible for managing my property.

After emails and calls failed to resolve matters, I attended their office seeking answers about my overdue payment. I was subsequently warned about police involvement if I attended the office again.

So my experience has included: late rent, changing payment dates, problems with bills and maintenance, ignored communications, an extremely difficult relationship with my property manager, contradictory explanations for unpaid rent and days taken off work simply trying to get matters resolved.

I strongly recommend that any landlord considering this company reads the lower-rated reviews for themselves before being persuaded by the initial sales pitch.

Keep everything in writing. Check every payment. Verify maintenance yourself. Document everything.

What started with a polished sales pitch became one of the most stressful business relationships I have ever experienced.

I am genuinely disgusted by how poor this item was.

First of all, the lamp itself was frankly horrible to look at in person. It looked cheap, unattractive, and nothing like the impression given by the photos. I bought it expecting a nice gold table lamp and was extremely disappointed the moment I opened it.

Secondly, the lamp did not even come with the bulb that was supposed to be included, which meant I could not actually use the product as delivered. I should not have to spend more money buying additional parts for a brand-new lamp just to make it functional.

Thirdly, the packaging made an unbelievable mess of my flat. The material inside the box went everywhere when I opened it and left the room absolutely filthy. I appreciate that some of the packaging or delivery process may involve Amazon or another delivery partner, but frankly I do not think that excuses the company. If you are selling products through a third party, you should have proper standards in place with your fulfilment and delivery partners so customers are not receiving items in this condition.

The whole experience was poor from start to finish: an unattractive product, incomplete contents, and packaging that created a huge mess in my home.

I would absolutely not recommend this lamp, and based on this experience I would be very reluctant to buy from Cinderella Lighting again. If you are considering this product, I would strongly suggest spending your money elsewhere.

Starting from the pick up was a sign of what this holiday was going to be like.
Picked up at 9am get to Tamworth services just after 10 which is where the main coach is. We didn’t even leave until 11:35 we then didn’t get the hotel until 8PM… just when we thought it was over we finally get in the hotel straight for dinner well i’d call it dinner for mice.
The portion sizes were tiny i thought it was a one off but all week it was tiny portions after tiny portions other than breakfast that was the only decent part. And food isn’t fresh it’s pretty easy to tell it’s majority frozen food but at least it was edible. But the most shocking one was probably the chicken and leak pie where the pie filling was put on the plate and then sat on top of the filling was a small plain puff pastry pie… no words besides salty, filling was like pure salt.
Now the hotel itself is well overdue a makeover, looks like it’s stuck 20 years in the past and the rooms are worse, tiny rooms, wallpaper peeling off, old furniture - doors are all chipped and dirty and a lovely bit of mould on the netting by the windows (see images) the bathroom was dirty too with bits of brown in the corners (see images). Oh and you can literally hear everything in the surrounding area, walls and doors are paper thin you can hear people in the other room opposite and next and even above when they’re walking around because everything is creaky and thin.
And the “excursions”
“Full day in Glasgow” was actually 3 hours in Glasgow, “Full day in Oban” was actually 2 hours 20 minutes in Oban. because the hotel is so far away from literally anything we have more time travelling to places than actually exploring it, more time sat on the coach than actually looking around the areas is just a joke.

If you are looking to do this specific holiday - don’t bother, i wish i could go back and tell myself not to book this and saved myself £500+ because this just wasn’t worth it at all.

Alex was offended and the conversation turned whereby she became condescending and talked over me constantly when asking some basic questions which anyone would ask. She said she'd see if she could get the figures to work and I asked why she'd need to do that as she already knew the price before calling me. i.e. you'd normally enquire about a car if in budget and rightly ask lots of questions about the car which she rightly and understandably did. You could then make a decision as to whether you then view the car and possibly then make an offer based on its condition. I simply wanted to understand why after asking to pay a deposit she said she'd need to check if she could make the figures work. She said she'd never been asked so many questions and was quite put out and to be honest, rude and talked over me, stating she'd been doing the job for 8 years! Again, I explained I totally understand her asking about the car and I would do the same but just was confused why she'd say she had to see if she could make the figures work after a call. Surely you'd do that beforehand. Given the company has a good rating, I suspect she may not actually work for this company and there may have been some sort of scam, or she just missed my point exactly. Either way she should play that conversation back if it was recorded and take some time to listen to the actual question. She explained that's how the company worked. A very unfortunate manner for a sales person seemingly acting as a buyer. Maybe next time just listen and understand the question before going off on one. Had she taken a pause and understood my question, and then adequately answered, there's a chance this could have progressed into a purchase/sale.

Response received a complete lie. A £100 deposit was offered very early in the conversation. **Absolutely appalling customer service. I would strongly advise potential buyers to think twice before purchasing from this company.**

I purchased a large, heavy table from this seller on eBay. Before they shipped it, they sent me a video of the actual table. The colour shown in the video appeared different the listing photographs, so I contacted them asking to cancel the order.

I messaged them requesting cancellation and also tried calling. They responded on WhatsApp acknowledging message (rather than eBay) and Instead of dealing with the issue properly, I was left asked to sort 2 days later on the Monday.

Despite already knowing that I wanted to cancel, they suddenly went ahead booking a courier to collect the table from their warehouse **before Monday** and shipped it to me anyway! They therefore had every opportunity to stop the delivery but chose to proceed.

The customer service I subsequently received was frankly disgraceful. I found the staff rude on the phone, so dismissive and completely unwilling to take responsibility for what had happened. During several telephone conversations, I was given information that was simply not consistent with what had actually happened, and I was repeatedly told things that I knew were untrue based on the messages and timeline I had in writing. Rather than acknowledge their mistake, the attitude was essentially to dismiss the problem and make it mine.

I am now being expected to return a **large and extremely heavy item**, which means paying a substantial amount for a courier. This is completely unreasonable given that I had already cancelled the order before they arranged collection and shipped it. It seemed more like a tactic in the hopes that I do not return the item so that they do not need to refund me.

This entire situation could have been avoided by simply listening to the customer and cancelling the order when requested. Instead, they ignored the cancellation, shipped the table anyway, and are now expecting me to deal with the consequences of their own actions.

The worst part is the appalling way they handled it afterwards: RUDE staff, terrible communication, dismissive, contradictory information and an outright refusal to accept any responsibility!

**A thoroughly unpleasant experience from start to finish. I would not buy from this seller again and would urge other buyers to avoid.**

I paid £250 for what has unfortunately been the worst haircut and colour experience I have ever had at a salon. I would not recommend this salon for colour, cutting, or any other service based on my experience.

Firstly, I booked a balayage/colour appointment and explained beforehand that I had around a year-old bleach and keratin treatment on the ends of my hair. Despite this, no strand test was carried out. A 6% developer was used, and the previously treated sections of my hair became severely damaged and turned to mush.

I understand that damaged hair sometimes needs to be cut, and I was completely accepting of having a long bob instead. My hair was just above my chest before the appointment, and I was prepared to lose length if necessary. However, the haircut I was left with was a completely separate issue.

The stylist was cutting away the damaged sections and I explained that I was happy to have layers. What I left the salon with was NOT a layered haircut. It was extremely choppy and uneven. I have survived COVID by cutting my own hair and somehow managed to keep it perfectly even, so I can genuinely recognise the difference when someone is confident and professional with scissors. Unfortunately, I did not see that level of professionalism here.

Before booking, I was also told that the package included a smoothing treatment. This was not used on my hair. My hair is naturally wavy, but after leaving the salon it was the frizziest and puffiest I have ever seen it — literally from the short walk from the salon to St Peter's Square. Even the blow-dry was disappointing. For a £250 service, I would expect basic professional products such as heat protection and leave-in conditioner to be used. The only product I noticed was some oil.

I specifically asked for a chocolate brown colour and was given a golden/red/caramel tone instead.

I contacted the salon and asked for both my haircut and colour to be corrected. When I returned, I was shocked to be told that I had asked for layers, as though this explained the result. Asking for layers does not mean asking for a choppy and uneven haircut. A professional should be able to distinguish between a layered haircut and an uneven/choppy cut.

The colour correction initially looked much closer to what I had requested in the salon, but unfortunately it washed out after the very first wash.

The haircut also looked better when the stylist blow-dried it after the correction, but once styled naturally, the underlying problems were still there. I have thick hair and actually had to tell the stylist to use texturising scissors. I was also very uncomfortable with the way the tool was being used, which further reduced my confidence in the service.

At this point, I have had to arrange for my own regular hairstylist to correct the haircut, meaning I will now have to pay additional money to fix a service I have already paid £250 for.

I have given the salon an opportunity to correct the issues, but unfortunately my hair is still not what I asked for and I am not happy with the result and I have wasted two Saturdays going to this salon!

I would not recommend this salon based on my experience.

I would now like a manager to contact me directly to explain the next steps for making a formal complaint and to discuss next steps.

After paying £250, I should not be in a position where I have to pay another hairstylist to fix my haircut and colour.

They said they had spoken to the sellers and that the date we gave was fine with them. However, their communication between buyers and sellers was awful, and we later found out that they hadn't told the sellers our preferred move date whatsoever, nor us the seller's, until one day, just days before Christmas, they rang us and told us the sellers were pulling out of the deal unless we bought it right away, that very day. In a single day, while my partner and I were at work, we were badgered and pressured all day long by Your Move to buy a house we couldn't yet afford, just so they could line their pockets a little more right before Christmas. As support workers caring for vulnerable and disabled individuals where our constant vigilence is sometimes life saving, the pressure and constant phone calls that day meant we couldn't do our jobs properly, and we were forced to leave work early to go and sort out whatever was going on. After a meeting with the agent, where we were spoken to and patronised like idiotic children, we very nearly told them where to stick the house, after they had threatened and messed us around in what should have been a very simple transaction. We ended up buying the house, and paying both rent/mortgage as well as bills for two properties for months (when we were only on part-time salaries).
We like our house, it's lovely, but we were less than impressed with how we were spoken to and treated that day, and if it comes to selling/buying again, we shall definitely, 100%, absolutely never use Your Move again.

P.S. Stop sending us emails about houses in our area! We don't care!

one_star_reviews.text:
Update:

I got a call last week, after over a year since my incident and was offered £100 as compensation after confirming with me that I indeed was owed £385 (recorded phonecall). With the "condition" being, I removed my review. I countered that until I was repaid the full amount, I could not edit my review as other people deserve to know the truth. I have not received any further contact. Make of that what you will 🙂

!!! DO NOT GO NEAR THE PLACE. THEIVING, SCAMMING CON MEN!!!

I bought a van from them on the 8th May,  viewed the van online where the van looked to be in good condition, and recieved video viewing as I lived 1.5 hours away. The apparently fresh MOT from May 1st was a complete fraud and has obviously been faked. It has a couple of advisories, which I was willing to deal with over the course of my ownership. I paid the full amount via bank transfer and added on a delivery fee of £180. On delivery of the van (a wholly unprofessional experience where the driver asked for a lift to the train station) I noticed many faults which usually would result in an MOT fail which were not advisories. Such as window wipers hanging off, seat belt buckle missing and extremely flat tyres, also back reverse light bulb dead.

I was willing to take the hit and sort these things myself so I could just move forward.

When I took the van to a tyre merchant he advised me the van was not safe to drive until I had it changed and it should never have passed MOT.

When I called the Direct Vans Bolton office about this, I was told I "could have picked up a nail anywhere". It was not a puncture but an extremely worn old tyre. They did reimburse me for the tyre initially, after I sent over an invoice for approval of the change at a local tyre merchant but then re charged ME for it during the refund process which is completely abhorrent behaviour and they now have a brand new tyre, against the law (theft).

Now extremely suspicious, I asked a mechanic to check the van thoroughly to spot any more shoddy work and give me enough time to return the van not even 5 days later, this is well within your rights as a consumer under the Consumer Rights act.

The seller, Zakki claimed he'd "checked the van before it left the lot" which suggests he's either a total fraud, and knew he was sending out a dangerous vehicle or completely incompetent and perhaps just thick?

On inspection my mechanic advised me the van was completely un road worthy and not safe to drive as the brake pads were in a dangerous condition, and the underneath of the van was completely rotten.

With videos, images and testimony from my mechanic I contacted DVB to request a return and a full refund. They advised they would only collect the van for an additional £200 collection fee. They insisted I either drove the van back to them. Or it was £200 !!! I couldn't safely drive the van on a motorway and this didn't seem to penetrate the sellers skull, until they clearly accepted I was right by sending a low loader to collect the heap of rust. I had cleaned the van, put on 2 new wipers, changed the tyre and bought a new liner for the back.

The radio didn't work properly either and the wheel arches were so rusty they were falling apart, the back had a rotten liner in and was full of 14 years worth of filth and they deducted yet another £160 as I had removed it to clean the van.

So not only did I recieve a complete dud they have charged me £385 for the privilege of a week's stress and reciept of a dangerous van. Even though under the law, I am not liable for the original delivery fee and this needs to be refunded.

They are criminals. They have clearly done this many times before based on the reviews and I am so relieved I got it inspected professionally well within my time limit. I have begun court proceedings to retrieve the outstanding amount.

I came back to Optegra specifically because I had previously met Fadi and felt completely comfortable and safe in his hands. I wanted him to perform my eye surgery, so I was prepared to wait.

Unfortunately, the experience since then has been extremely disappointing.

Even more frustratingly, I was told there was no record on the system of the finance arrangement I had previously set up.

I have also experienced problems getting prescriptions and getting calls returned during the process.

I fully understand that prices can change and that different lenses may cost more. My complaint is about the lack of communication. A change of this size should have been clearly explained before I travelled back for my appointment, particularly after I had already been through the finance process and waited months to proceed.

I eventually walked out of the appointment because I felt I was being presented with the new price without a satisfactory explanation of what had happened.

This is particularly disappointing because my confidence in Fadi himself was the reason I chose to return to Optegra in the first place.

I would strongly recommend avoiding this letting agency. Before the tenancy began, they were very helpful with arranging viewings and answering questions. When the tenancy started, there were a few issues: one of the backdoor keys were missing; some of the previous tenants’ items were still in the house, including a soiled mattress which made one bedroom unusable; the washing machine was full of mouldy and unusable. A condition of renting the property was that the garden was to be cleaned and tidied. While the garden waste was cleared, the glass and rubbish was left in the garden. The letting agency was informed of these issues.

It took several months and a formal complaint for the washing machine to be replaced. Needing to use the second bedroom, the mattress had to be moved outside. Despite being told that it would be removed along with the previous tenants’ items, it stayed there for the entire tenancy. The other rubbish in the garden was never removed. It took over 6 months for the backdoor keys to be made.

The letting agency was informed about damp and mould which had begun to form in an upstairs room and in the kitchen - both caused by leaks. Several contractors were sent (sometimes the same one twice) to give quotes. A contractor was finally sent to fix the leaks over 6 months later but the remaining damp/mould was not treated. When I left the property it was still there.

During the tenancy, I spoke to many people from the letting agency and property management company over email and phone. I had to follow up on every issue, otherwise no one would get back for over a month. Any time I would bring it up, I was told they were still waiting for the landlord - no progress had been made at all. If the landlord was the one at fault, it seems like they should stop working with clients like this. Although many of the letting agents/property managers apologised for the situation, there was never any improvement.

AVOID!!! Extremely pushy sales process — make sure you understand exactly what you’re agreeing to.

I would actually have been perfectly happy to advertise with Fieldway and, had the service worked, I could easily have remained a customer for longer than 24 months. Unfortunately, the way this was sold to me has completely put me off the company.

The advertising I responded to stated £5 + VAT per week. I then paid £312, genuinely believing this was the cost of the advertising package I was buying.

I subsequently discovered that Fieldway considered me committed to a minimum 24-month contract at £260 + VAT every quarter — effectively £20 + VAT per week.

That is a massive difference from how I understood the offer that attracted me in the first place.

I found the sales approach extremely aggressive and pushy. I never signed or returned the agreement, never approved the artwork, and asked to cancel before my advert was published. Despite this, following our discussions, Fieldway’s position is that I cannot simply get out of the 24-month commitment.

What frustrates me most is that none of this was necessary. If I’d been offered a straightforward advertising service at a clearly explained price without what I consider an aggressive long-term commitment, I would gladly have used them and potentially stayed for years.

Instead, I am now having to dispute a 24-month agreement that I do not believe reflects what I understood I was buying.

My advice to any business considering Fieldway: read absolutely everything, ask for the TOTAL cost and minimum commitment in pounds before paying anything, and do not rely solely on the headline weekly price.

I’ve attached the actual advert I responded to. It clearly states “FOR ONLY £5 + VAT PER WEEK”. You can make your own mind up about how that offer comes across.

I understood the £312 I paid to be the cost of the advertising being offered. Fieldway’s position is that I actually committed to £260 + VAT every quarter for a minimum of 24 months — equivalent to £20 + VAT per week.

That difference is exactly why I am disputing this.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very frustrating experience with the Post Office service at this branch.

I had a Royal Mail parcel redirected here for collection. At 13:03 on Saturday I received an email confirming that the parcel had been successfully delivered to the collection point, and I arrived at the branch at around 13:30.

The shop itself was open normally, and the Post Office’s own website showed the branch as open on Saturdays from 7am–9:30pm, with services available at the branch.

I went to the counter, said I was there to collect a parcel and gave the member of staff my name. He then began looking through the parcels behind the counter. After he was unable to find mine, he told me that the Post Office was actually closed and that I would have to come back on Monday.

Only after leaving did I notice a printed notice on the door saying the Post Office was closed due to “unforeseen circumstances”.

I completely understand that unexpected closures can happen. What I don’t understand is why the closure was not reflected anywhere customers could reasonably check before travelling. Royal Mail had confirmed my parcel had been delivered there less than half an hour earlier, while the Post Office’s own website was still showing the branch as open.

I also found the interaction with the member of staff quite dismissive. He had already started searching through the parcels before telling me the Post Office was closed, and there was no apology or acknowledgement at all that I had made a wasted journey based on the information provided by Royal Mail and Post Office.

If the branch is unexpectedly unable to provide Post Office services, that really needs to be reflected promptly in the online information and, ideally, in the systems used for parcel collections. A notice on the door only tells customers once they have already wasted their time getting there.

Hopefully this is something that can be improved so other customers don’t have the same experience.

Myself and my Partner purchased a Grandland X from Evans Halshaw in January 2026. Upon having the car 4 months the oil pressure light came on, I phoned my trusted garage explained the oil light and the message and they advised the wet belt needed replacing. I took the car in for repair and received a phone call to say that the wet belt wasn’t the issue, the issue was debris was blocking the oil filter and had entered the engine. They advised a new engine was needed as a new wet belt was a temporary fix. I then phoned Evans and spoke to a manager who agreed for me to bring the car in and they would investigate. A report with photographic evidence along with the faulty parts was left in the car upon drop off. All they did was put a new wet belt on. I had the car back 8 days before the oil pressure light came on and I discovered an oil leak. At this point I’d had enough of having to tell the manager and the rest of the staff at evans that the car needed a new engine. We then decided to reject the vehicle and I was eventually given a courtesy car. It took weeks for us to even get a figure off the manager for what money we’d be getting back. The service we received from Evans was unacceptable. There was no communication at all in regards to the car or about our refund. It wasn’t until i threatened legal action that we finally received the refund for the car. We was also promised the money back for the towing fee. This never arrived until I spoke to a different manager and explained that the car had been put on the website without the rest of the payment being received. He was was the only member of staff who I dealt with who sorted my issue quickly. I’d avoid buying a car from these and also avoid buying the car unless you want a hefty bill for a new engine.

We purchased a Vauxhall grandland 20 plate from Evans halshaw in January. We had the car for around 6 months with no issues however after 6 months the oil pressure light came on the dashboard. We took the car to another garage and was informed the wet belt needed replacing which we were prepared to pay for as the car was out of its warranty period.
The garage then contacted us and explained that there was a bigger issue in that the wet belt had been replaced recently but the sump wasn’t cleaned out which meant it was highly likely that it had gone into the engine.

We approached Evans about this issue under the consumer rights act, after a lot of back and forth they agreed to correct the issue. We were told that the issue was the wet belt and that the engine was fine, however this was not the case. The oil light then reappeared a week or two later so we took the car back and rejected it. The rejection was accepted, however communication was a nightmare. We kept being told that the manager would phone us back as he’s busy, the phone calls never came. We finally took the car in after around 3-4 weeks of chasing to be told the money would be transferred within 7 days. We waited nearly two weeks for the car refund and then had to chase for the money we paid out for the car to be towed which took a further two weeks.

Went to Silverlake today with my partner and visited the salvage yard out back, where we removed a DPF from a car. We then went to the counter to pay. The gentleman serving us was lovely and, to be clear, we have absolutely no fault with him. He told us the price was £35, so we were happy with that, paid for the part and were given a receipt.

The gentleman next to him then asked whether it was a catalytic converter. My partner explained that it was a DPF, not a catalytic converter. We were then told that it couldn’t be sold to us, despite the fact that we had already paid for it and had a receipt confirming the transaction.
He went out the back to speak to his colleagues about it and returned to say they could sell it to us for £250 rather than the £35 we had already paid. The way this was communicated to us was also extremely rude and left us feeling very uncomfortable.

We completely understand that Silverlake has policies regarding the sale of catalytic converters. However, this was a DPF, and we had already paid the advertised/quoted price and received a receipt.
We were therefore very disappointed that the transaction was subsequently changed and that we were ultimately unable to take the part home.
We had no issue whatsoever with the gentleman who initially served us — he was polite and helpful throughout. Unfortunately, the way the situation was handled afterwards was very disappointing, and we left feeling extremely frustrated after what should have been a straightforward transaction.
It is also worth pointing out that Silverlake has prices for DPFs listed online, which makes the situation even more confusing. If DPFs are advertised and priced through Silverlake’s own website, we don’t understand why we were told that the DPF we had already paid for at £35 could not be sold to us, only to then be offered it for £250.

I really wanted to give this company the benefit of the doubt, but unfortunately my second experience with them has been even more disappointing than the first.

Last year, I had a wool coat dry cleaned here. When I collected it, it was still dirty. After a long period of contacting them and getting no response, I was eventually offered a re-clean, which did resolve the issue. I gave the company the benefit of the doubt and decided to use them again months later.

This time, the service has been shocking from start to finish.

I booked a collection for Monday, and selected a drop of for Wednesday. I stayed home all day specifically so I wouldn’t miss it the pick up but nobody turned up. After calling, I was told someone would come later that evening, which they eventually did.

After that, I received multiple random notifications changing the expected delivery date. Eventually the delivery date had passed while the order was still showing as “cleaning”. I contacted them to ask when my dress would actually be ready and was simply told that they were “working on the stains”, with no indication of when it would be completed.

Over a week later, my card was charged, without my consent, even though it says online that “you will only be charged upon drop off”.

On the delivery day, once again nobody turned up and I wasted another entire day waiting. When I contacted them, I was eventually told there had been a power cut. Again, nobody had thought to notify me. I had to chase them to find out what was happening and even then had to exchange multiple messages with them to understand when my delivery will be.

The dress was eventually delivered the following day. When I opened the bag, I was absolutely shocked to find that it was essentially in the same dirty condition as when I handed it over.

I immediately sent photos and asked for an explanation, particularly because they had kept the dress for two weeks and had specifically told me they “were working on the hem stains”. If the stains could not be removed, I would have expected them to simply tell me that. Instead, I was charged for a service that clearly hadn’t been provided.

Their response was simply that they would “contact the store”. There was no apology or acknowledgement of the inconvenience I had already experienced, and I heard nothing further for 3 days.

I chased them one final time asking for an explanation and a proposed resolution, voicing my frustration about me having to chase them constantly. They offered to collect the dress that afternoon so that it could be personally inspected, but no acknowledgement or apology was given.
I agreed and, (I can’t even make this up at this point) despite giving them yet another opportunity to put this right, nobody turned up to collect the dress.

At this point, I genuinely don’t know what more I could have done as a customer. I have now lost money, valuable time and a huge amount of time and energy waiting around for missed collections and deliveries, repeatedly chasing for updates and trying to resolve an issue that shouldn’t have required this much effort in the first place. It has also caused completely unnecessary stress over a dress that’s sentimental for me.

So, in summary: missed collection, repeated changes to delivery dates, no proactive communication, an unexpected card charge without consent, a missed delivery, another day wasted waiting, a dress returned still visibly dirty after being in their possession for around two weeks, another lack of communication, and then a further missed collection when they offered to rectify the problem.

I am genuinely very disappointed. I don’t tend to leave reviews, and I try and give companies the benefit of the doubt, and opportunity to rectify mistakes. However, the amount of opportunities I’ve given this company is just wild, and each time the service, communication and customer service have been extremely poor.

I agreed a sale on my property to a first-time buyer who already had their mortgage offer agreed in principle and who instructed Amity Law to act for them.

The draft contract package was emailed to Amity Law on the same day the sales memorandum was issued.  We then went through a very stressful and frustrating four months with Amity Law seemingly very rarely being prepared to communicate with my Lawyer, my Estate Agent and even often Amity Law's own client!  When we were nearly four months in, I was then told they were only then reviewing their client's evidence for their source of funds, which should have been done at the start of the process as if there were issues with that, the deal would not have been able to proceed.  That review apparently took over a week!  In desperation, as I was told my buyer would soon be away on work commitments for several months and which was likely to jeopardise the whole deal, I rang Amity Law myself.  (Not being their client, I knew they would not speak to me but hoped that they may listen to me and the experience I was told everyone else involved was having with Amity Law).  Finally, the sale was transferred to another Conveyancer in their organisation and "flagged up" as urgent, it then finally exchanged and completed little time later, but in a very short timeframe, leaving very little time for me to clear my property.

For some context, the property was a relatively modern freehold house which had been conveyed numerous times over the years and on a development of several hundred other homes.   When I had purchased it in 2001, I was ready to exchange contracts three and half weeks after I had agreed the deal and when I had not even applied for a mortgage until we had agreed the terms.  I and my Solicitor did not do anything magical, we just got on with the process and communicated with everyone involved. it's really quite simple!

I give this advice as someone who previously spent about twenty years as an Estate Agent and who has dealt with numerous conveyancing businesses such as Amity Law and has sadly seen this experience time and time again.  Do not use the seemingly "good value" conveyancing service offered by a mortgage lender's recommendation or which you have found elsewhere and which seems like a good deal, it is a false economy and may jeopardise your whole sale/purchase.  They are generally paid relatively little and in turn, very often provide precious little service/communication, causing everyone involved a great deal of additional stress.  Use a Solicitor or Licensed Conveyancer who you have either had a good personal experience with or one who has been recommended by someone you know who has used them or indeed by the Estate Agent involved and who is not earning commission from their recommendation.  I never received any payment from the Solicitors or Conveyancers I recommended but only did so on the basis of the experience I had of them and knew they would get on with the process and would actually communicate with all parties concerned.

Extremely Slow, Poor Communication, and Unreasonably High Fees.
I had a very frustrating experience with Amity Law, particularly with Alison. Their communication was poor and the entire process moved at an unacceptably slow pace.
My first transaction with them had to be withdrawn after we discovered high service charges during enquiries. When I returned with a new property, their quoted fees went up significantly. On top of the higher quote, they caused severe delays and immense stress by making unreasonable demands, such as requiring 4 years' worth of bank statements for source of funds checks—far beyond standard requirements.
Due to the lack of responsiveness, extreme delays, and escalating costs, I had to ask them to close my case and switch to a different conveyancer. Switching away made me realize how efficient and supportive home buying service should actually be.

I reported a safety concern to HSE after works at a premises in Baslow blocked the pavement with an access tower and barrier tape, forcing me into a busy road. I completed their online form and supplied photographs.

What followed was a series of emails apologising for delays. HSE then requested further information, including details I’d already supplied, and gave me until 5pm the following day to respond, warning that their ability to act could otherwise be limited. After their own repeated delays, that deadline was particularly frustrating.

When I explicitly complained, I was directed to a complaints webpage. A manager subsequently apologised and confirmed that my original evidence had been reviewed, that they had enough information to proceed, and that the concern remained open. However, there was still no assessment outcome or firm date for one.

I wasn’t expecting an automatic prosecution or a particular enforcement decision. I expected a timely assessment, clear communication and reasonable treatment of someone who had taken the trouble to report a risk.

This experience has completely destroyed my motivation to report safety concerns to HSE again. If you want members of the public to help identify dangerous situations, the reporting process needs to make that effort feel worthwhile. Mine has left me feeling that it was a waste of time.

I am writing to express my serious concerns regarding the standard of service at Tesco Pharmacy in Bulwell, Nottingham. My recent experiences have consistently demonstrated a lack of professionalism, poor communication, and an absence of customer-focused care.

Each time I attend the pharmacy to collect a prescription for my elderly mother, who is in her late nineties, the medication is not ready—despite following the collection instructions provided by her GP. When raising this issue, I have been told that although doctors advise patients to collect prescriptions the next day, the pharmacy requires up to 48 hours to process them. This discrepancy leaves vulnerable patients without essential medication and causes unnecessary distress.

The attitude of some staff members often feels dismissive, as though customers are an inconvenience rather than individuals seeking important medical support. There is little sense of empathy or urgency, even when the situation clearly involves pain or discomfort for the patient. Communication is minimal, and on several occasions I have been left waiting without acknowledgement while staff wait for the pharmacist to authorise medication, despite being visibly present.

Although seating is provided near the counter for busy periods, the manner in which concerns are handled—often with abrupt or unhelpful responses—creates an environment where customers feel undervalued and ignored. It is disheartening to experience this repeatedly, especially when caring for an elderly parent who relies on timely access to medication.

Overall, the service at this pharmacy does not reflect the standards expected from a healthcare provider, and I hope these issues can be addressed to ensure a more respectful, efficient, and compassionate experience for all customers.
